description: We are JSS Sol Seekers, a team exploring how interactive games can make space science easier for young people to understand. We created Red Horizon to help kids learn about the difficult choices involved in keeping a Mars outpost running.
summary: I created Red Horizon, a browser-playable Mars outpost game that helps young players explore real mission trade-offs. Over seven Martian days, players balance oxygen, power, and shielding while deciding whether to build a dust shelter, conduct science, tend a food garden, or send a science report to Earth. Each plan uses resources, and the mission log shows how choices affect the crew.
details:
Red Horizon is a browser game that helps children ages 7–12 understand the decisions involved in living on Mars. Players follow a crew from rocket launch to a seven-sol outpost mission. Before landing, they choose between spending power on extra sensors for an earlier warning in the game, or saving more power for the habitat. After landing, they choose one daily plan: build a soil shelter, explore for science, tend a food garden, or send a message to Earth.

Each choice affects the crew’s supplies. Science outings and gardening use oxygen and power; shelters use power; crops and messages take time to produce results. The game’s resource points, storm timing, and two-sol communication delay are simplified teaching mechanics, not real mission predictions or astronaut safety limits.

The project uses NASA information for context. It shows a historical Curiosity rover radiation measurement of about 210 micrograys per day from its early Mars surface observations, and a NASA DONKI panel for solar-particle reports when available. DONKI is not connected to the game’s simulated storm. The NASA image and data sources are credited in the game.

Red Horizon aims to make mission planning easier to understand through play. Instead of only reading facts, students experience how protecting the crew, using power, doing science, and communicating can compete with one another. The launch story, changing event timing, and replayable choices make it suitable for individual or classroom play.

The game is built with HTML, CSS, and JavaScript as a browser-based page, so it can be played without downloading an app or creating an account. No special hardware is required. JSS created the Red Horizon name and original game concept. ChatGPT assisted with brainstorming the flight-plan choice, drafting some mission narration, and editing the game code. The AI-assisted parts are disclosed in the project’s SI-use section.
